bottleneck: NGRAM greedy correctness is BUG_CONFIRMED (canonical F1) and no promotion is possible. Static CPU fault-line work on this branch (t3 mask-contract audit and no-op _sanitize_tree_mask guard; t4 topology/accept-index/KV-mover oracle; t5 single-request mask-width oracle) has excluded the corpus mask causality, the root/bonus convention, the accept-index bookkeeping and the KV-mover compaction conditional on a valid root. The one live NGRAM-specific surface left from t3 item 1 was the verify-window KV read/pack alignment. t5 tested it for a single request only; the FA2 CUDA-graph path actually packs a FLAT batched mask whose per-request block offsets come from device-cumulative widened lengths while the mask is BUILT from host per-request seq_lens_cpu widths, so with bs>1 a per-request host/device drift can cross-contaminate other requests.
hypothesis: H-CPU-4 (new): the NGRAM verify custom-mask packing pipeline (ngram_worker.py:352-361 build with host h_i -> ngram_info.generate_attn_arg_prefill:76-117 device-derived mask_numel and global True padding -> flashinfer_backend.py:263-285 device-cumulative packed_indptr -> pack_verify_mask.py:12-24 block read at kv_start*Q) is bit-exact if and only if h_i == d_i for EVERY request in the batch, not merely per request. If any request drifts, all later blocks in the same flat buffer shift even when those later requests are themselves aligned, and no assertion fires (the only check is packed_indptr[-1] <= buffer numel, and a short mask is silently True-padded). The drift itself is NOT claimed reachable: the FutureMap audit (G3-i3) argues host and device mirrors are equal by construction, so the expected outcome is a sharper latent-hazard negative and a batch-level falsifier, not the F1 root cause.
patch: No engine change. New pure-stdlib CPU oracle ngram_oracle/verify_window_oracle.py plus raw ngram_oracle/results/verify_window_oracle.json and write-up ngram_oracle/README-verify-window.md. It hand-ports the builder layout ([D rows][h_i+D cols] prefix-ones + causal tree rows, global True padding/truncation to device mask_numel), the packer's device-cumulative block offset and (d_i+D)*D-bit block count, and compares each delivered (row,col) mask bit against the intended mask. Scenarios: fully aligned three-request batch; mid-batch drift (req1 d=6 h=5); first-request drift (req0 h=5 d=4). Existing t4/t5 artifacts are unchanged and not re-derived. HEAD still carries t3's no-op _sanitize_tree_mask guard only.
tests: Executed locally: python3 -I ngram_oracle/verify_window_oracle.py ngram_oracle/results/verify_window_oracle.json, exit 0, stdlib only, no GPU/provider/evaluator. Results: aligned 32/32, 36/36, 40/40 bits exact (all requests exact); mid-batch drift req0 exact, req1 18/40 bits wrong (first row0 col9 expected 0 delivered 1), req2 16/40 bits wrong although req2 is itself aligned (first row1 col2 expected 1 delivered 0); first-request drift all three requests wrong (12/28, 16/36, 16/40). No exception raised in any scenario; summary.cross_request_contamination=true. This is a new negative relative to t5: the hazard propagates across requests through the flat mask buffer. NOT requested: no GPU/fast gate (request_fast_gate=false) because this trial ships no engine change and unchanged HEAD's BF16 fast screen cannot advance the NGRAM fault line. NOT_TESTED: real Triton pack kernel, FlashInfer FA2 custom-mask consumption, CUDA-graph buffer capture/replay, server.log; reachability of h_i != d_i on hardware.
learning: Bounded CPU negative finding with a new batch-level component: the NGRAM verify custom mask is exact only if host and device prefix lengths agree for every request, because the builder writes host-width rows while the packer reads device-cumulative blocks. A drift in one request corrupts later requests' mask bits (req2 16/40 wrong while aligned), which is a stronger, multi-request version of the t5 single-request width hazard. Under the documented FutureMap equality the assembly is exact (aligned scenario), so this remains a latent hazard and a falsifier, not the F1 root cause: reachability of drift is unproven, and the first-diff positions 4/6 fit a persistent width drift poorly. Limitations: pure index/bit arithmetic; the delivered-bit mapping assumes the documented row-major (d_i+D) column contract; the real kernels, graph replay and live overlap timing were not executed. No throughput, quality, EXACT or promotion claim is made; NGRAM stays non-promotable.
next_proposal: Make the hazard observable in one controller-run batch-pinned ON/OFF probe instead of a whole-source sweep: add a log-only counter at _prepare_for_speculative_decoding comparing, per request, the host prefix used for ones_masks against the device widened paged_kernel_lens in the same forward (requests-differing, total delta, and the global mask_numel vs raw built numel), emitted to server.log and a small JSON; the same probe also records accept_lens==1 to close the t3/t4 accept-path discriminator. Decision rule: any non-zero drift on real requests -> width/block-shift class confirmed, fix the host-mirror source (or fail closed on mismatch) and re-run the ALGORITHM_PRESERVING probe; zero drift with divergence reproduced -> this class is excluded and the remaining live surface is runtime KV-window ordering (previous verify's KV vs the widened CSR read) plus graph-replay buffer maturity, which needs an in-kernel trace. Prefer bundling with the existing probe; do not gate NGRAM on throughput until it is ALGORITHM_PRESERVING.
